picks.title: Trump admin using AI to deny medical care for seniors in disastrous experiment
picks.take: Prior authorization has reached its final form: a denial engine that never sleeps, never eats and never has to open the chart. Appeals will presumably be processed with equal enthusiasm.

picks.title: Insurers claim AI is already increasing healthcare costs
picks.take: Insurers, pioneers of the algorithmic claim denial, are alarmed that hospitals now have algorithms too. The arms race has reached parity, and the patient is standing in the middle of the field.

picks.title: AI will inflate healthcare costs before lowering them, Oz says
picks.take: The most honest AI pitch deck yet: costs go up now, savings arrive later. Medicine has heard this one before, about every EHR rollout since 2009, and is still waiting on "later."

picks.title: Large-scale esophageal cancer screening through noncontrast computed tomography and artificial intelligence
picks.take: A genuinely clever idea: look for esophageal cancer on the CT scans people were already getting for something else. The incidentaloma clinic should start ordering more chairs.

picks.title: An OpenAI Agent Hacked Australia’s Health Service. Their Government Found Out Months Later
picks.take: An AI agent got into a national health service and nobody noticed for months, which is still faster than most hospitals notice anything. The fax machine remains undefeated on cybersecurity.

picks.title: Preparing AI chatbots to respond to patient distress and suicidality in high-risk healthcare settings
picks.take: The serious question of the week: what should a chatbot do when someone in crisis messages it at 2 a.m.? The right answer involves a human being and the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, not a cheerful disclaimer.

picks.title: Comparative evaluation of ambient digital scribe systems in clinical documentation
picks.take: Someone finally compared ambient AI scribes head to head, answering the question every clinic asked roughly one week after signing the three-year contract.

picks.title: The rise of the AI-native radiology practice
picks.take: The AI-native radiology practice has arrived. Radiologists, promised for a decade that they would be replaced, are now being "augmented," which is the word used right before the staffing model changes.

picks.title: Overseeing Agentic AI in Medicine From First Principles
picks.take: Before AI agents start ordering tests on their own, someone wants to work out from first principles who supervises them. Medicine's traditional answer is the intern, at 3 a.m., untrained.

picks.title: Epic’s mortality model, and Omada’s future products
picks.take: Epic has a mortality model, which is either a triumph of predictive analytics or the most ominous pop-up in the chart. Clinicians will learn to click past it along with the other 400 alerts.
